audit.whatIsWrong: Chart reads Skill, Kayle, Kayle, Skill, Skill, Kayle, Kayle. The mel__kayle audit already landed the inverse chart on the other side — Mel, Mel, Skill, Skill, Kayle, Kayle, Kayle — and the packet agrees. The page also labels this EVEN at 6/10 while the mirror set its own side to TRICKY 6.5/10 and left an explicit instruction that this file must land at 3.5/10 to stay the inverse.
audit.why: Mel is a 950-range area poke mage against a melee Kayle for three levels; the flip is Divine Ascent at 6, not level 2. Leaving the chart as-is would make the two pages disagree on four of seven rows and mirror-fix would overwrite it anyway.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-1 set to Mel, row 2 to Skill, row 4 to Kayle — four matched full/content pairs. diff set to FAV, diffRating to 3.5/10, tone to the favoured colour, with the two prose fields that quote the number updated to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rebuttal is described only as a 'reflect window - don't dump a big auto into it'. It reflects projectiles back at the caster AND prevents her taking damage, and every damaging thing Kayle owns — Radiant Blast, Starfire Spellblade, and her ranged-form autos — is a projectile. Searing Brilliance and Overwhelm are never mentioned at all.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction and the mirror auditor named it from the other side: firing Radiant Blast into Rebuttal returns the poke and hands back the resistance shred. 'Don't dump a big auto' understates it — a Kayle in ranged form pouring autos into the barrier is shooting herself. And Overwhelm means chip you shrug off is stored damage her ultimate cashes later, which changes whether you can afford to eat poke.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal restated with its 38s rank-1 cooldown, the projectile reflection, and the fact that Kayle's whole kit is projectiles. Searing Brilliance's bonus-projectile tell (the cast, not the autos) and Overwhelm's banked damage written into early.

audit.whatIsWrong: Solar Snare is named the matchup-defining cooldown throughout with no number, and Rebuttal's cooldown — the longest and most punishable timer in her kit — appears nowhere.
audit.why: Rebuttal at 38s is the window the lane is actually won in: once it is spent she has no damage prevention for over half a minute. Solar Snare at 11s is the timer that gates every step-up.
audit.corrected: 38s and 11s written into mid and dosFull[0].d.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Solar Snare and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 3.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Rebuttal and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 6/10, Mel carry threat 8/10.

Levels 4-5 stabilize as your second W point and Q's armor/MR shred come online, but you're still trading at a range deficit - play for farm, not kills. Level 6 is the flip: Divine Ascent turns your autos into ranged AoE waves and Divine Judgment hands you a few seconds of invulnerability, so now you match her range and her poke stops mattering. Watch her W (Rebuttal) reflect window - don't dump a big auto into it - and be ready to dodge her E root that sets up her damage; otherwise auto her down with E (Starfire) extending your range while her health melts under your waves.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stabilize as your second W point and Q's armor/MR shred come online, but you're still trading at a range deficit - play for farm, not kills. Level 6 is the flip: Divine Ascent turns your autos into ranged AoE waves and Divine Judgment hands you a few seconds of invulnerability, so now you match her range. Respect Rebuttal (38s at rank 1): it blocks damage and reflects projectiles back at you, and Radiant Blast, Starfire and your ranged autos are all projectiles. Never fire into the barrier - wait it out, dodge the E root, then melt her through the downtime.

edits.before: Mel out-ranges you hard for the first three levels and her Radiant Volley poke is the entire threat - you have melee autos, only Q for poke and one point of W to heal, so you cannot trade back. Don't walk up to throw a Q she can sidestep while she free-pokes you; last-hit at the tip of your Q range and use W only when you actually need the heal, not to bait poke. The saving grace is she has no hard engage - her kit is area poke, a reflect window, and a root, with no gap-close to convert your low HP into a kill, so eating chip is survivable as long as you don't walk into her E snare.
edits.after: Mel out-ranges you hard for the first three levels and her Radiant Volley poke is the entire threat - you have melee autos, only Q for poke and one point of W to heal, so you cannot trade back. Every ability she casts loads bonus projectiles onto her next attack, so the cast is your cue to step out, not the autos that follow. Her damage also stacks Overwhelm for her ultimate to cash in, so chip you shrug off is damage banked against you. Last-hit at the tip of your Q range; she has no gap-close, so low HP alone will not kill you if you stay out of the E snare.

edits.before: Her root / slow zone — sets up her combo. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Her root and slow zone, 11s at rank 1 — dodge the orb, then engage while it is spent.

notes: Mirror-driven. The mel__kayle auditor left an explicit handoff: their side is TRICKY 6.5/10, and this file 'must land at 3.5/10 to stay the inverse'. Done, along with diff EVEN->FAV and the matching tone, plus the two prose fields that quote the difficulty number so the page does not print 6/10 next to a 3.5/10 badge. Chart set to the inverse of the mirror's atomic group. Their point-4 finding — hold Rebuttal for Radiant Blast, because the reflect returns both the poke and the resistance shred — is restated here from Kayle's side and extended: every damage source in Kayle's kit carries the projectile flag, so ranged form pouring autos into the barrier is the worst version of the same mistake.
